description: Estimate prior probabilities from occurrence data, habitat, and spatial modeling

functions.name: build_priors
functions.description: High-level wrapper: GBIF fetch -> habitat -> grid -> model -> priors -> backbone translation

inputs.name: taxa
inputs.description: Data frame with taxonomy rank columns. Column names encode the rank (family, genus, species). IMPORTANT: the prior algorithm estimates sampling effort from multiple species captured by similar methods. A single target species is insufficient — provide a broader group (e.g. data.frame(family = 'Gobiidae') or a multi-species list) so the algorithm can gauge how well-sampled each grid cell is.

inputs.name: lat
inputs.description: Latitude of study site

inputs.name: lon
inputs.description: Longitude of study site

inputs.name: rank_system
inputs.description: Taxonomy ranks

inputs.name: habitat_scheme
inputs.description: Habitat classification: NULL (default 3-category: Marine/Freshwater/Terrestrial), 'IUCN_L1' (18 IUCN Level 1 groups), or a custom data.frame with an l1_name column listing the habitat categories (e.g. data.frame(l1_name = c('Estuarine', 'Freshwater', 'Rocky Intertidal', 'Sandy Subtidal'))). If the user provides habitat names, construct a custom data frame.

inputs.name: llm_fn
inputs.description: LLM provider for habitat assignment

inputs.name: geographic_context
inputs.description: Geographic hint for habitat LLM

inputs.name: target_backbone_id
inputs.description: Target backbone for translating prior taxon names (4 = NCBI, 11 = GBIF). Does not affect the GBIF occurrence query itself.

inputs.name: year_range
inputs.description: GBIF year filter as a comma-separated string, e.g. '2000,2024'. NULL (default) returns all years. Must be a string, NOT a numeric vector.

inputs.name: search_radius_deg
inputs.description: Radius in degrees around site for GBIF search. Larger values (5-6) provide more grid cells for the spatial model and produce much better species-habitat differentiation. Values below 3 often produce too few grid cells for the model to estimate species-specific habitat slopes.

inputs.name: supplemental_occurrences
inputs.description: Additional occurrence data to include

inputs.name: verbose
inputs.description: Print progress messages

output.description: List with $priors (data frame with grid_id, main_habitat, taxon_name, theta) and attributes

functions.scaling_note: GBIF + LLM + modeling; 10-60 min depending on taxon count and geographic scope

functions.name: optimize_grid_size
functions.description: Find optimal spatial grid resolution for prior estimation

inputs.name: observation_data
inputs.description: Occurrence data with coordinates

inputs.name: n_covariates
inputs.description: Number of model covariates

inputs.name: lat_col
inputs.description: Latitude column

inputs.name: lon_col
inputs.description: Longitude column

inputs.name: species_col
inputs.description: Species column

inputs.name: habitat_col
inputs.description: Habitat column

functions.name: prepare_model_dataframe
functions.description: Prepare gridded occurrence data for biodiversity model fitting -- computes per-taxon presence/absence and shared effort denominator (n_total_at_site) per grid cell

inputs.name: data
inputs.description: Gridded occurrence data with grid_id, lat_r, lon_r, habitat_col, taxon_name

inputs.name: covariates
inputs.description: Spatial covariate columns

inputs.name: habitat_col
inputs.description: Habitat column; NULL disables habitat modeling

inputs.name: cor_threshold
inputs.description: Drop a covariate if correlated above this with another

inputs.name: sampling_group_col
inputs.description: Column identifying which detection PROCESS/METHOD each row belongs to (e.g. 'fish' vs 'birds' vs 'phytoplankton'). When supplied, n_total_at_site is computed group-aware (split-and-recombine internally) so effort isn't pooled across incomparable sampling processes. NOT the same as a physical site/spatial_group_id

output.description: Data frame ready for compute_moran_basis()/train_biodiversity_model() (or train_biodiversity_model_by_group() when sampling_group_col was supplied)

functions.name: train_biodiversity_model_by_group
functions.description: Fits one biodiversity model PER sampling_group_col value instead of pooling every taxon into one model. Required when data spans multiple detection processes with different effort -- train_biodiversity_model() itself refuses multi-group data

inputs.name: data
inputs.description: Raw gridded occurrence data (NOT pre-processed by prepare_model_dataframe() -- this function re-derives model data per group internally)

inputs.name: formula
inputs.description: Model formula, typically from screen_spatial_formula()$formula run once on the full/combined data

inputs.name: sampling_group_col
inputs.description: Column identifying detection process/method groups. Required -- for ungrouped data use train_biodiversity_model() directly

inputs.name: covariates
inputs.description: Spatial covariate columns

inputs.name: habitat_col
inputs.description: Habitat column

inputs.name: taxon_col
inputs.description: Taxon column

inputs.name: response
inputs.description: 'theta' or 'psi'

inputs.name: min_obs_threshold
inputs.description: Minimum observations to attempt a group fit

inputs.name: effort_threshold
inputs.description: Minimum total effort to attempt a group fit

inputs.name: min_positive_rows
inputs.description: Minimum positive-detection rows to attempt a group fit

output.description: Named list of biofreq_model objects, one per sampling_group_col value. Groups that fail to fit (too sparse) are dropped with a warning, not an error

functions.scaling_note: One model fit per group; seconds to minutes depending on number of groups

functions.name: generate_domestic_food_priors
functions.description: Adds named Beta(alpha, beta) prior rows for domestic/commensal animal species, human food/crop species, and (optionally) candidate cultivated plants -- a non-GBIF prior source using live iNaturalist casual-grade evidence, for the gap where occurrence-database indexing structurally under-counts captive/cultivated organisms. Output is bind_rows()-compatible with generate_full_priors()'s taxaexpect_priors

inputs.name: model_obj
inputs.description: Output of train_biodiversity_model() (or one element of train_biodiversity_model_by_group()'s list); used only for N_total and habitat_col so these rows sit on the same theta scale as the rest of taxaexpect_priors

inputs.name: lat
inputs.description: Query site latitude for the iNaturalist search

inputs.name: lng
inputs.description: Query site longitude for the iNaturalist search

inputs.name: grid_id
inputs.description: Grid cell identifier attached to every output row, for joining into taxaexpect_priors

inputs.name: domestic_animal_taxa
inputs.description: Domestic/commensal animal taxon names. Default is a pre-populated starting list (dog, cat, cow, sheep, pig, chicken, horse, Homo sapiens, etc.). Set to character(0) to disable this channel

inputs.name: food_species_taxa
inputs.description: Human food/crop species taxon names, a separate contamination category from domestic_animal_taxa (food-handling/lab-bench contamination, not pet/livestock). Default is a pre-populated starting list. Set to character(0) to disable

inputs.name: candidate_plant_taxa
inputs.description: Candidate plant-kingdom taxa (e.g. from your study's own plant-kingdom BLAST/GBIF matches) to check for real local cultivated/casual-grade iNaturalist evidence. Default NULL (channel disabled, no live iNaturalist calls made unless supplied)

inputs.name: radius_km
inputs.description: iNaturalist search radius

inputs.name: taxonomy
inputs.description: Optional taxon_name + rank columns (incl. kingdom) joined onto the result. Supplying a kingdom column enables an iNaturalist cross-kingdom-homonym check

inputs.name: api_token
inputs.description: iNaturalist API token; defaults to the INAT_API_TOKEN environment variable

output.description: One row per resolved domestic/food/plant taxon: taxon_name (always populated, unlike generate_undetected_diversity()'s anonymous proxies), grid_id, alpha, beta, theta_mean, theta_sd, model_tier ('tier_domestic_food'), prior_source_type ('domestic_animal'/'food_species'/'domestic_plant'), inat_n_observations_local, inat_kingdom, inat_kingdom_mismatch

functions.scaling_note: iNaturalist API; seconds to ~1 min depending on how many candidate_plant_taxa are supplied
